questions.stem: What type of quantity is distance?
questions.explanation: Distance is a scalar quantity because it has magnitude only and does not include direction.

questions.stem: A runner completes one full lap of a 400 m track, returning to the start. What is their displacement?
questions.explanation: Displacement is the straight-line distance from start to finish. Since the runner returns to the starting point, the displacement is 0 m.

questions.stem: Which statement about distance and displacement is correct?

options.text: Displacement can be negative but distance cannot
Distance is always equal to displacement
Distance includes direction but displacement does not
Displacement is always greater than distance

questions.explanation: Displacement is a vector and can be positive, negative, or zero depending on direction. Distance is a scalar and is always positive or zero.

questions.stem: A student walks 30 m east, then 40 m north. What is the magnitude of their displacement?
questions.explanation: Using Pythagoras' theorem: displacement = sqrt(30^2 + 40^2) = sqrt(900 + 1600) = sqrt(2500) = 50 m.

questions.stem: Under what condition is distance equal to the magnitude of displacement?

options.text: When the object returns to its starting point
When the object moves in a straight line without changing direction
When the object moves in a circle
Distance is always equal to displacement

questions.explanation: Distance equals the magnitude of displacement only when the object moves in a straight line without changing direction, so the total path length equals the straight-line distance.

questions.stem: What is the SI unit for both distance and displacement?
questions.explanation: The SI unit for both distance and displacement is the metre (m). Kilometres and centimetres are derived from metres using SI prefixes.

questions.stem: A person walks 10 m north, then 10 m south. What is their total distance travelled?
questions.explanation: Distance is the total path length: 10 m + 10 m = 20 m. Note that displacement would be 0 m since the person returned to the start.
